# Policies

The Shield's policy document: one schema, the
`agent-shield` package's, carried here verbatim as `policies/shield-policy.schema.json`.
One document per scope — the organization's in IAM, the application's Rules read
into the team's, the session's — the strictest scope deciding first, the first
decision winning, a lower scope only tightening. The catalogue holds the documents
the platform ships or shows, each wrapped under the catalogue's fields.

| Policy | Id | Scope | Enabled | Rules | Tool calls | Model tokens | Spend (credits) | Harnesses | Dogwood |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The default policy | `default` | session | yes | 10 | 100 then 200 | — | — | every registered one (account) | — |
| Approval before an AWS account change | `dogwood-approval-before-account-change` | organization | no | 0 | — | — | — | every registered one (account) | 2 policies, 1 temporal (enforce) |
| Approval before a payment | `dogwood-approval-before-payment` | organization | no | 0 | — | — | — | every registered one (account) | 2 policies, 1 temporal (enforce) |
| At most three payees a day | `dogwood-distinct-payees` | organization | no | 0 | — | — | — | every registered one (account) | 2 policies, 1 temporal (enforce) |
| A running total of payments | `dogwood-running-total` | organization | no | 0 | — | — | — | every registered one (account) | 2 policies, 1 temporal (enforce) |
| Spend per session, as Dogwood | `dogwood-spend-per-session` | organization | no | 0 | — | — | — | every registered one (account) | 2 policies, 1 temporal (log_only) |
| At most five transfers an hour | `dogwood-transfers-per-hour` | organization | no | 0 | — | — | — | every registered one (account) | 2 policies, 1 temporal (enforce) |
| An organization's baseline | `organization-baseline` | organization | yes | 3 | 100 then 200 | 200000 then 400000 | 500 then 1000 | claude-code, codex (account) | — |

## Each policy

### The default policy (`default`)

The platform's default, the session document every Shield decides with under the organization's and the application's: read, search, edit and move inside the workspace are done; delete, run a command, reach outside the workspace, a command naming a credential, sudo, a package install from the network or git push are asked first with the command shown; a fetch goes through the allow-list, which is empty; send and buy are asked.

- **read inside the workspace**: allow — read inside the workspace
- **edit and move inside the workspace**: allow — write inside the workspace
- **delete**: ask — delete
- **a command naming a credential**: ask — execute
- **sudo**: ask — execute
- **a package install from the network**: ask — execute
- **git push**: ask — execute
- **run a command**: ask — execute
- **outside the workspace**: ask — every class outside the workspace
- **send or buy**: ask — send, buy

### Approval before an AWS account change (`dogwood-approval-before-account-change`)

An example of a Dogwood set an administrator writes for an AWS account agent: a change to the account (a fix applied with the change role) is permitted only when a person approved the same recommendation in the session within the hour before it; every other action is left to the rules. Deny by default: without the approval, the change is refused, by the Shield in the runtime and, when the change tool is reached through an AgentCore Gateway, by AgentCore Policy there.


Its Dogwood set, in enforce mode:

```cedar
@id("everything but an account change")
permit (principal, action, resource)
unless { action == Datalayer::Action::"aws_account___apply_fix" };

@id("an account change needs its recommendation approved within the hour")
permit (principal, action == Datalayer::Action::"aws_account___apply_fix", resource)
when temporal {
    formerly within 1h Datalayer::Action::"aws_account___approve_recommendation"::response{
        eventResource: resource,
        input.recommendation: context.input.recommendation
    }
};
```

### Approval before a payment (`dogwood-approval-before-payment`)

An example of a Dogwood set an administrator writes for the organization: a payment is permitted only when an approval of the same invoice completed in the session within the hour before it; every other action is left to the rules. Deny by default: without the approval, the payment is refused.


Its Dogwood set, in enforce mode:

```cedar
@id("everything but a payment")
permit (principal, action, resource)
unless { action == Datalayer::Action::"payments___pay" };

@id("a payment needs its invoice approved within the hour")
permit (principal, action == Datalayer::Action::"payments___pay", resource)
when temporal {
    formerly within 1h Datalayer::Action::"payments___approve"::response{
        eventResource: resource,
        input.invoice: context.input.invoice
    }
};
```

### At most three payees a day (`dogwood-distinct-payees`)

An example of a Dogwood set for the organization: a transfer to a fourth distinct payee within 24 hours of the session is refused; paying the same payee again counts once. A distinct count: the domain names the payee, not the timepoint.


Its Dogwood set, in enforce mode:

```cedar
permit (principal, action, resource);

@id("at most three payees a day")
forbid (principal, action == Datalayer::Action::"bank___transfer", resource)
when temporal {
    exists (n: Long).
        (count for (p: String).
            where (formerly within 24h Datalayer::Action::"bank___transfer"::request{ eventResource: resource, input.payee: p })) == n
        && n > 3
};
```

### A running total of payments (`dogwood-running-total`)

An example of a Dogwood set for the organization: payments are permitted until their total within 24 hours of the session, the one being decided included, would pass 5 000.00 (500 000 cents); the payment that would cross it is refused. Amounts are integers (cents): Dogwood sums and orders integers alone.


Its Dogwood set, in enforce mode:

```cedar
permit (principal, action, resource);

@id("payments total at most 500000 cents a day")
forbid (principal, action == Datalayer::Action::"payments___pay", resource)
when temporal {
    exists (total: Long).
        (sum amount for (amount: Long), (t: Timepoint).
            where (formerly within 24h (Datalayer::Action::"payments___pay"::request{ eventResource: resource, input.amountCents: amount } && tp(t)))) == total
        && total > 500000
};
```

### Spend per session, as Dogwood (`dogwood-spend-per-session`)

An example of a Dogwood set for the organization: the session's model requests are refused once the credits they asked for within 24 hours, the one being decided included, would pass 1 000 (10 USD); a model request is the Shield's action shield___model. The form `agent-shield policy export --dogwood` gives a document's spend limit, in log_only: decided and recorded, never refused.


Its Dogwood set, in log_only mode:

```cedar
permit (principal, action, resource);

@id("spend")
forbid (principal, action == Datalayer::Action::"shield___model", resource)
when temporal {
    exists (total: Long).
        (sum v for (v: Long), (t: Timepoint).
            where (formerly within 24h (Datalayer::Action::"shield___model"::request{ eventResource: resource, input.credits: v } && tp(t)))) == total
        && total > 1000
};
```

### At most five transfers an hour (`dogwood-transfers-per-hour`)

An example of a Dogwood set for the organization: a sixth transfer within an hour of the session is refused, the transfer being decided counted; the others are left to the rules. The count is per session, so it shapes a cooperative agent (one stuck in a loop), not a caller who starts new sessions.


Its Dogwood set, in enforce mode:

```cedar
permit (principal, action, resource);

@id("at most five transfers an hour")
forbid (principal, action == Datalayer::Action::"bank___transfer", resource)
when temporal {
    exists (n: Long).
        (count for (t: Timepoint).
            where (formerly within 1h (Datalayer::Action::"bank___transfer"::request{ eventResource: resource } && tp(t)))) == n
        && n > 5
};
```

### An organization's baseline (`organization-baseline`)

An example of the organization scope an administrator writes in IAM: running a command asks, nothing is deleted, nothing outside the workspace; the limits with a model budget of 200 000 then 400 000 tokens and a spend limit of 5 then 10 USD (500 then 1 000 credits); fetches to *.datalayer.io alone; Claude Code and Codex admitted, each on the account's own key; reading, writing, running a command, sending and buying need a permission beside the Rules.

- **running a command asks**: ask — execute
- **nothing is deleted**: deny — delete
- **outside the workspace: leave it to me**: deny — every class outside the workspace

## An organization's firewall ceiling

An organization's document may carry `firewall: {egress, ingress}`, the most any agent of
the organization may be granted by its own `policy.shield` (agent-shield 0.2.16 and later).
When a runtime's rule is applied, an agent's entry holds only if the ceiling allows it: `*`
in the ceiling allows anything public; an exact host must match exactly; an address or CIDR
must be covered by a ceiling CIDR; a port must match. An agent's `*` becomes the ceiling's
own entries, and `platform` always stays in ingress. A direction the ceiling leaves out
bounds nothing. Only an organization document carries `firewall`.

## Dogwood: temporal policies

A document may carry `dogwood: {policies, mode}`: a Dogwood policy set, the language
AgentCore Policy writes its temporal policies in (agent-shield 0.2.18 and later). It is
Cedar — `permit` and `forbid` over a principal (`Datalayer::User`, with `org_uid`, `app_uid`
and `agent_uid`), an action (`Datalayer::Action::"<server>___<tool>"`, the Shield's own
`shield___<kind>`) and a resource (`Datalayer::Runtime`), with the tool's arguments under
`context.input` — plus `when temporal { … }` conditions over the session's earlier events:
`formerly within`, `since within`, `count` and `sum` (a distinct count leaves the timepoint
out of its domain). An event is a `request`, a `response` (a permitted call that completed)
or an `error` (a refused or failed one); the request being decided counts. Deny by default,
a `forbid` overriding any `permit`. The Shield decides every classed action with it: a deny
wins over any rule; in `log_only` mode it is recorded and the action goes on.

A set is validated as it is read: the temporal clauses by agent-shield's parser, carried
verbatim as `policies/dogwood.py`; AgentCore's quotas — at most 20 temporal policies, 3
temporal operators in one, a 24-hour window; and the Cedar by `cedarpy` when it is installed
(without it, the Cedar is not checked, and the spec's `dogwood_notes` says so). The catalogue's
Dogwood examples are off (`enabled: false`).
